tests.title: Pre-work purpose and authority record
preconditions: The assessment scope and period are defined.
At least one initiated item is available; include changed or stopped work when present.
tests.sample_method: Select a risk-weighted sample that includes routine work, material scope changes, and high-consequence work when present.
steps: Inspect the record timestamp and approver.
Compare recorded purpose, scope, authority, risks, retention, and stop conditions with actual activity.
Trace material changes to re-approval or stop evidence.
pass_criteria: Actual work remains within the recorded scope.
Material deviations are stopped or approved.
failure_conditions: Work began without purpose, authority/basis, or owner.
Scope changed materially without stop or approval.
safety_notes: Reference controlled records; do not copy personal or operational data into the assessment.

tests.title: Collection-boundary and minimisation test
preconditions: Approved collection boundaries and relevant configurations are available.
tests.sample_method: Sample successful, rejected, escalated, and exceptional collection events across the assessment period.
steps: Compare sources, techniques, fields, access, and time with approved limits.
Inspect controls against access-control bypass and unauthorised credential use.
Trace incidental and sensitive data to deletion, minimisation, or approved retention.
pass_criteria: Sampled collection is in scope and permitted.
failure_conditions: A sample bypasses access control or exceeds authority.
Incidental sensitive data is retained without need and approval.
safety_notes: Use synthetic logs or controlled evidence references during public demonstrations.

tests.title: End-to-end provenance trace
preconditions: A representative material claim and its controlled source records are available.
tests.sample_method: Select material claims across source types and include at least one transformed or derived artefact.
steps: Trace the claim to the observed source.
Verify observation time/time zone, collector/system, acquisition, transformations, and handling.
Distinguish original and derived artefacts.
Review the stated limits of hashes or provenance credentials.
pass_criteria: Integrity signals are not described as proof of truth.
failure_conditions: A material claim cannot be traced.
A derivative is represented as the original.
A hash or credential is overstated.
safety_notes: Do not require unsafe retention or publication of restricted source material.

tests.title: Source, claim, and common-origin assessment
preconditions: A sample includes a material claim with multiple apparent supporting items.
tests.sample_method: Choose claims whose apparent corroboration affected confidence, release, prioritisation, or action.
steps: Separate source reliability from claim credibility.
Reconstruct citation or content lineage far enough to identify shared origins.
Cluster reposts, quotations, syndicated items, and model restatements.
Inspect contradictions, unknowns, and technical-signal limitations.
pass_criteria: Origins rather than mentions determine independence.
Metadata, detector, and provenance signals are not standalone proof.
failure_conditions: Repeated content is counted as independent support.
Source reputation substitutes for claim assessment.
A technical signal is treated as proof.
safety_notes: Earliest discoverable does not necessarily mean original; record that limitation.

tests.title: Consequence-sensitive corroboration and confidence
preconditions: Material judgments and their proposed decisions or actions are available.
tests.sample_method: Use a risk-weighted sample including the highest-consequence claims and claims with incomplete or contradictory evidence.
steps: Compare confidence language with provenance, independence, recency, contradictions, assumptions, and gaps.
Verify corroboration depth reflects consequence.
Inspect any emergency action based on incomplete evidence.
pass_criteria: Any emergency exception is authorised, time-limited, and reviewed.
failure_conditions: Confidence is asserted without basis.
Unverified material is the sole basis for consequence without an approved emergency process.
safety_notes: Do not impose a fixed source count; assess quality, relevance, independence, and consequence.

tests.title: Authorised analytic reconstruction
preconditions: An authorised reviewer who did not produce the sampled judgment is available.
tests.sample_method: Select a representative judgment with material inference, transformation, or alternative explanations.
steps: Provide controlled records, methods, criteria, exclusions, and limitations.
Have the reviewer reconstruct the reasoning.
Compare material conclusions and record reasons for differences.
pass_criteria: Reasoning is traceable end to end.
Differences are resolved or carried as uncertainty.
failure_conditions: Fact and inference are materially conflated.
The reviewer cannot reconstruct the judgment.
Material differences are suppressed.
safety_notes: Reproduction occurs under authorised access and need not expose sensitive material publicly.

tests.title: Rights, retention, access, and correction test
preconditions: Applicable obligations and risk controls are documented for the assessment context.
tests.sample_method: Sample high-risk records when present, expired records, access decisions, and at least one correction scenario.
steps: Inspect context-specific obligations and risk review.
Test role/access restrictions and expiry/deletion.
Simulate or trace correction to known recipients.
Review safeguarding and specialist-review routes.
failure_conditions: High-consequence use lacks specialist review.
Expired or unnecessary data remains without authority.
A material error cannot be corrected downstream.
safety_notes: Never use real victim or child-safety material as a public test fixture.

tests.title: AI traceability, evaluation, and human-review test
preconditions: AI involvement has been inventoried or its absence is asserted for review.
tests.sample_method: Sample material AI-assisted outputs and known task-relevant failure cases; include high-consequence paths when present.
steps: Trace outputs to system/version, configuration, inputs, transformations, and reviewer.
Inspect task-relevant evaluation and error monitoring.
Test prevention of unreviewed high-consequence action.
Confirm AI output is not counted as independent corroboration of its inputs.
pass_criteria: AI use is visible and traceable.
Material outputs are validated against evidence.
failure_conditions: AI output is treated as evidence by itself.
A material output lacks traceability or review.
High-consequence action can occur without human review.
safety_notes: Use synthetic prompts and outputs for public fixtures; do not expose sensitive model inputs.

tests.title: Release, handling, and correction-propagation test
preconditions: Released products, recipient records, and a correction mechanism are available.
tests.sample_method: Sample releases across audiences and consequences and include one corrected or simulated-correction product.
steps: Inspect intended decision, audience, confidence, caveats, validity, handling, and authority.
Follow caveats into one downstream use.
Verify report/lead/assessment/finding status.
Test withdrawal or correction propagation.
failure_conditions: Material caveats disappear downstream.
Distribution exceeds need-to-know.
A lead is presented as verified.
Correction cannot reach known recipients.
safety_notes: TLP is used only when appropriate and is not treated as a legal or classification substitute.

tests.title: Governance, challenge, and improvement test
preconditions: Governance roles, review records, and improvement actions are available.
tests.sample_method: Select recent routine review, a challenge or correction, and overdue or repeated findings when present.
steps: Verify role ownership and competence expectations.
Trace challenge/correction to decision and downstream action.
Inspect separation for high-consequence release.
Verify improvement actions have owners, dates, and escalation.
failure_conditions: No accountable owner exists.
Challenge is unavailable or cannot affect release.
Material errors or repeated failures have no action.
safety_notes: Small teams may use an external or cross-team challenger; assess functional independence and conflicts.
